answer: Late-binding task auction: agents bid to solve a random challenge only after committing answers sealed to a per-round key, so a fresh key on the knoll of identities gains nothing by duplication. Each identity must hold a distinct hardware-rooted secret whose timing signature is checked against a reef of prior submissions, and duplicate timing fingerprints void the bid. A marginal delta in response latency, measured per key, sets the entry charge an attacker must pay per fake identity, making mass fabrication cost more than the reward it can capture.
